text: Can you squeeze a rock into a smaller space? No. Can you squeeze water? Also no. But a gas? Yes! One simple squeeze test helps tell solids, liquids and gases apart.

Hi there, and welcome to The One App, Explained! I'm so happy you're here. Today, you will learn three big ideas. First, what a solid is. Second, what a liquid is. And third, what a gas is, and which one can be squeezed. Let's get started!
Matter can be in three states. Solid, liquid or gas. Scientists sort them using two questions. Does it have a definite shape? And does it have a definite volume?

Solids first. A hammer keeps its shape, whether it is on a table or in a toolbox. It has a definite shape, and a definite volume. You cannot squeeze it into a full toolbox, because solids cannot be compressed.
Now liquids. Pour tea from a teapot into a jug. The tea takes the shape of whatever holds it. So a liquid has no definite shape.

But it does have a definite volume. Pour a full jug into a small cup, and it overflows, because liquids cannot be compressed. Pour it into a huge teapot, and it does not fill it up. That is why a water shooter works. Push the water, and it has to squirt out.

Finally, gases, like air. Pump air into a basketball, and it takes the ball's round shape. And you can keep pumping more air in, because gases can be compressed. A gas has no definite shape and no definite volume. It spreads out to fill all the space it is given.
Try it with a syringe. Pull the plunger, and air fills the space. Cover the nozzle and push, and the air squeezes into a smaller space.
Squeezing gas is very useful. A scuba diver carries a tank of compressed air, so lots of air fits on their back. And helium is squeezed into tanks, ready to fill party balloons of any shape.
Look at our planet. Solid rock, liquid oceans, and a layer of air. All three states of matter, in one place.
Pause and predict! Which one has a definite volume, but no definite shape? A marble, milk, or air?
Milk! It is a liquid. A marble is a solid, with a definite shape and volume. Air is a gas, with neither.

In your exam, say it like this. A solid has a definite shape and a definite volume. A liquid has no definite shape, but has a definite volume. A gas has no definite shape and no definite volume. Solids and liquids cannot be compressed, but gases can.
Here is a habit trick. Use a habit tracker. Draw a row of boxes, one for each day. Every time you revise, tick a box. Watching the chain of ticks grow makes you want to keep it going.

Now your mind map. States of matter in the middle, with three branches. Solid, liquid and gas. For each one, write whether it has a definite shape, a definite volume, and whether it can be compressed. Save it in TheOneApp, the ultimate science app.
So, which state passes the squeeze test? Only gas! Your turn. Find one solid, one liquid and one gas in your kitchen. Which one could you squeeze?
Thanks for watching! See you next time. Bye!
